summary: Koki Kawagishi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University, both attested in 1976.
Konrad Klaus is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Michael Hahn from circa 1978 to 1985. He taught Bruno Galasek and held a post at the University of Bonn around 1993.

Kosei Ishii is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1970–1982) and later worked there. He served at Komazawa Junior College (~1993–2005) and held a professorship at Komazawa University (~2005–2021).

Kosei Mizutani was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University (~1948–1952). He served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1961–1970) and later as president (~1981–1989).

Kosei Tada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1966). He held a post at Taisho University (~1982–2009) and served as board chairman of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (attested 2004).
Koshin Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and served as a researcher there, attested from 1995 to 1998.

Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940). He held posts at Toyo University, Tohoku University, Nihon University, and the University of Tokyo.

Kosho Kawamura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He later held several academic posts at Toyo University (~1957–1994).
Kosho Uchiyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1932–1937) and under Kodo Sawaki (~1941–1965), whom he succeeded. He taught Shohaku Okumura.

Kotatsu Fujita was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard. He taught at Hokkaido University (~1968–1991) and served as head of Sapporo Otani Junior College (~1991–1995).
Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post at Taisho University from circa 1952 to 1974.

Koun Yamada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School (~1924–1927) and Tokyo Imperial University (~1927–1930). He succeeded Hakuun Yasutani, taught Ruben L. F. Habito, and worked at NOF Corporation (~1941–1969).
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.

Koyu Tamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University and Toyo University, serving as professor at the latter (~1970–2002).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who earned M.A. degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Oxford. He served as Principal at Jagannath Barooah College (~1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Hare School and Presidency University, Kolkata. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and Bishop's College, Kolkata (attested 1869–1870).

Krishnanath Chatterjee is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amareshwar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.
Kristin Scheible is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Colby College and Harvard University. She taught at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College (attested 2008).

Kristina Myrvold is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She worked as an editor (attested 2005) and was a Ph.D. candidate (attested 2008) at Lund University, and later served as Assistant Professor at Linnaeus University (attested 2014).
